newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin to return to Moscow next Tuesday - Tass.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin to return to Moscow next Tuesday - Tass.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin will return to Moscow next Tuesday after a month-long summer vacation in which he has kept up a busy schedule of political meetings, Itar-Tass news agency said on Friday.
The president, on holiday at the Volga river resort of Volzhsky Utyos in central Russia, held talks on Friday with Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin and Russian central bank governor Sergei Dubinin.
Yeltsin's talks with Chernomyrdin had focused on army reform and payment of wage arrears to the military and state sector workers, Interfax news agency said.
"Everything is going to plan here, on schedule, is being taken positively by the military themselves," Interfax quoted Yeltsin as saying.
Earlier this week he urged the military rank-and-file to support far-reaching reforms aimed at turning the huge, cash-strapped army into a leaner, more efficient fighting force.
Yeltsin told Interfax he would give an account of his conversation with Dubinin on national television and radio "in a few days". He gave no further details.
The 66-year-old president, who has received a steady stream of officials during his vacation, named Ramazan Abdulatipov as a new deputy prime minister in charge of nationality issues.

Abdulatipov, from the Caucasus region of Dagestan, is a former political opponent of Yeltsin. "But in recent years he has supported the course of the president and government," Interfax quoted Yeltsin as saying.

Yeltsin, who has made a strong recovery from open heart surgery and pneumonia last winter, began his vacation on July 6 at a lakeside resort in the northwest region of Karelia near the Finnish border and moved to Volzhsky Utyos two weeks ago.
Despite keeping up a heavy workload, he has managed to enjoy his hobbies of fishing, hunting and tennis and has made regular visits to the sauna.
Yeltsin faces a busy autumn schedule, with planned visits to the French city of Strasbourg on October 10-11 to address the Council of Europe summit and later to China and Sweden.

He is also expected to receive a number of foreign visitors, including the presidents of Turkmenistan and Armenia in August and Germany's President Roman Herzog, Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi, Egypt's President Hosni Mubarak and French President Jacques Chirac in September, Tass said.
